Subject: Quick Qs on routing, subprocessors, and deletion attestations

Hi Sean —

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. Before we move this through procurement I need a concise Q&A that we can hand to our security and legal teams. Specifically can you confirm the following for hosted API traffic originating from our US region: 

1) Precise execution footprint — which cloud regions may process requests and for what stages (inference, logging, telemetry).
2) Which subprocessors handle ephemeral tokens, request payloads, logs, and long-term backups?
3) Do you have proof-of-deletion timelines (tombstone + overwrite) we can include in our privacy appendix?
4) For customers on Dedicated vs Hosted, how does cross-border behavior change (if at all)?
5) Are audit logs or immutable telemetry ever exported outside the US (and to which subprocessors)?

If you can attach a residency matrix, subprocessor inventory (CSV), and a SOC2 snapshot that would be great. Tom and I will consolidate and come back with any redlines.

Appreciate a reply by Wednesday EOD if possible — we have a security review on Thursday.

Best,
Lucy
Director, Infrastructure Security
Archway Health

Hi Lucy / Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, followed by attachments and a few clarifying notes. I looped in Kimberly (security) and Marissa (solutions) to provide the evidence and more detailed timelines.

Summary answers (short):
- Execution footprint: For US-origin traffic we execute inference primarily in us-west-2 and us-east-1. We maintain failover capacity in eu-west-1 for scheduled maintenance only; cross-region routing happens only when a region is unavailable or as part of a configured multi-region redundancy policy (customer opt-in).
- Subprocessors: We use a small set of subprocessors for storage, logging, and monitoring; listed in the attached CSV. Ephemeral KV cache remains in-memory on the inference host by default; request payloads touch short-lived object storage for batching windows (usually <24 hours) on AWS in the region above.
- Deletion/tombstone: Hosted: tombstone + 30 days soft retention for rollback, then automatic overwrite/secure-delete processes within 90 days depending on media. Dedicated: can be configured to shorter SLOs (30 days total) and supports customer-managed KMS. Private (VPC/on-prem): data stays on customer-managed infra unless you opt into Redwood-managed backups.
- Audit logs: Aggregated telemetry and anonymized metrics are retained for operational observability; full immutable audit logs are stored in a US-only bucket by default but may be delivered to customer-owned S3 in another region on request.

I attached the residency matrix, subprocessor inventory, and SOC2 snapshot for your security review. Kimberly and Marissa — can you expand the technical evidence and provide a short attestation we can send to Archway?

Next steps: if you want a one-pager attestation signed by our security team we can provide that + DocuSign for the DPA amendment. Happy to jump on a quick call if any of the answers need more detail.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Hi Lucy —

Following up with the technical evidence you requested. I've attached a zipped evidence packet (subprocessor-evidence-Archway.zip) with redacted contracts, subprocessor SOC pointers, and an export of our subprocessor chain for the last 12 months. Below are explicit answers and exact SLOs so your reviewers don't need to interpret high-level prose.

1) Execution footprint (detailed)
- Inference: Primary execution sites for US-origin requests are us-west-2 (primary) and us-east-1 (secondary). Failover to eu-west-1 only occurs if both US zones are unavailable and if the customer's routing policy allows failover.
- Logging/Telemetry: Short-lived logs (request traces, debug logs) are written to regional object storage in the same region as the inference host. Aggregated telemetry is forwarded to our centralized telemetry cluster (US region) for alerting and anomaly detection; raw traces are truncated by default to remove PII within 48 hours.
- Backups: Long-term backups (snapshots used for model versioning and recovery) reside in US-only encrypted buckets unless customer opts into global replication.

2) Subprocessors (role-by-role) — see attached CSV for full list; highlights below:
- Storage: AWS S3 (us-west-2 primary) — handles short-lived payload staging and long-term backups for hosted customers.
- Observability: Datadog (US tenant) — receives aggregated, pseudonymized metrics.
- Logging pipeline: Confluent Kafka (managed) operated in us-west-2 — intermediate streaming, with offsets retained per the retention policy.
- Encryption KMS: Customer-managed KMS supported for Dedicated; Redwood KMS (HSM-backed) used for hosted logs and snapshots.

3) Deletion timelines and attestations
- Hosted API customers: soft-delete/tombstone on request within 24 hours; logical deletion propagation within 30 days; physical media overwrite or crypto-erase within 90 days. The exact final deletion step depends on medium (ephemeral NVMe vs S3 object).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): we provide configurable deletion windows; default contract SLO is 30 days end-to-end for request/workspace artifacts when configured with customer-managed keys.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood does not perform cross-border copies unless you opt into Redwood-managed backups; deletion behavior is controlled by customer infrastructure.

Evidence we can provide for your package:
- Signed attestation of the deletion SLOs (we can sign a one-page security attestation).
- Export of subprocessor contracts and SOC references (redacted).
- Audit log snapshots (we can deliver a downloadable archive to a customer-owned S3 bucket, US-only by default).

4) Cross-border specifics & export gateways
- We do not route production request payloads to EU or APAC except in two scenarios: (a) customer enables multi-region replica/failover, or (b) a specific region is unavailable and the customer policy allows emergency failover. 
- We operate a tight export gateway policy: any cross-border move of persistent data requires an internal approval workflow and is logged to our immutable export ledger (retained for 2 years).

5) Immutable logs & audit exports
- Immutable audit logs (write-once append-only) are kept in a US-only account for hosted customers unless you ask us to export to customer-owned storage. We can place an export lock and provide attestations for retention windows and storage location.

Attached: subprocessor-evidence-Archway.zip (bundle), residency-matrix.pdf, subprocessor-inventory.csv, SOC2-snapshot.pdf

If you need a DPA clause or signed evidence, I can prepare the attestation and hand off to legal. Marissa, please take note for the procurement packet.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Compliance, Redwood Inference
